fixture_name: Ramp-terminal arterial reconstruction — US preliminary design (MassDOT HSIP municipal RSA, full package)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Ramp-terminal pedestrian crossings, a four-lane high-speed mid-block crossing, vegetation-limited visibility, non-compliant signage, and a recorded past fatality are core substantive safety issues squarely relevant at preliminary design for an interchange scheme.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claims are anchored in recorded site observations (Safety Issue #4: crossing deficiencies, vegetation, signage, fatal collision) plus verbatim quotes EV-US-030 (separation-failure mechanism) and EV-US-032 (signing/marking duty) that directly support the concern and requirement.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly typed as a safety_concern under FHWA RSA semantics; MUTCD/ADA references serve as supporting treatment criteria rather than converting the finding into a compliance item, and evidence uses (supports_concern vs defines_requirement) are properly distinguished.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Recommendation is specific, staged (immediate signage, current-design ramps/crosswalks, future signalized ramp crossings), and viable including relocation to the Derby Shoppes signal with sidewalk extension—no null or vague elements.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians are explicitly identified as the directly exposed vulnerable user group with their exposure mechanisms (crossing ramp traffic, divided driver attention) analyzed; drivers included as interacting users.

justifications.substance: Undefined lane drop with abruptly terminating striping, absent advance signage, and observed late merges at the ramp mouth create a genuine expectancy/conflict hazard between merging and ramp-exiting drivers — substantive for a preliminary-design RSA.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim (abrupt striping termination, no signage) is supported by verbatim quote EV-US-033; the observed late-merge behavior is a recorded field observation from Safety Issue #2 rather than invented content, with EV-US-023 framing RSA scope.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern arising from design/operational characteristics consistent with FHWA RSA purpose (EV-US-023); no compliance question conflated, and null normative_basis_note is appropriate for a non-code safety issue.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: advance merge signage and pavement markings ahead of the on-ramp, plus a viable alternative (extending two through lanes beyond the ramp with mandatory-right-turn trade-off signed in advance) carried into the ongoing reconstruction design.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrian exposure at the adjacent mid-block crosswalk is explicitly acknowledged, the driver-attention interaction mechanism identified, and impacts properly delegated to dedicated finding JB-GF12-001 while the vehicle-vehicle mechanism is correctly scoped to drivers.
